question: Which next experiment is most likely to improve the deployed Connectome ensemble after accounting for adaptive validation reuse, training-seed variation, and CPU inference cost?
deliverables: repair methodology problems 1-3 in repository skills
independently proposed and reviewed hypothesis cards
bounded CPU screens with reproducible artifacts
ranked next experiments with explicit uncertainty
metric: mean of two global pooled Pearson correlations; target and prediction clipped to [-2,2]; weights abs(clipped target); exact need_prediction AND is_scored mask
evaluation_unit: whole continuous chain; never independent rows

data_exposure.folds_2_3: previously inspected for width and fine-tuning; not untouched
data_exposure.old_holdout: inspected and used in final fitting; not untouched

uncertainty.chain_bootstrap: conditional on fixed fitted models; sampling uncertainty only
uncertainty.training_seeds: matched repeated training needed for recipe effects
uncertainty.adaptive_selection: no significance or unbiased confirmation claim from reused folds

scope.data: existing organizer data and prediction caches on beleriand

registration: Commit candidate specification, comparison, readouts and stopping rule before each screen; append results separately. Any post-result change is a new exploratory attempt.

promotion.this_iteration: rank next experiments only; no submission promotion or replicated-effect claim
promotion.next_training_screen: fixed recipe and epoch; paired candidate/control seeds; compare deployed ensemble contribution; report seed and chain uncertainty separately
promotion.confirmation: genuinely unexposed data if available; otherwise state exploratory status and use prospective external evaluation without retroactive retuning

stop: no discriminating screen without new heavy training
invariants: no true past-label feedback unless exactly reconstructible by that time
no edits to existing running jobs or shared caches
no claimed causation from predictive association
no OLS, LARS, temporal-placebo or universal-Sharpe veto without task-specific justification
